impact_assessment.why: persistent standing order: measure faster than C, C++ and Rust on every benchmark case; the recorded losses are the remaining gaps
impact_assessment.benefits: C++ baseline measured and gated; the remaining loss mechanisms (call overhead, frame pressure, merge scheduling) become failing-first byte tests before any codegen change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: benchmark twin parity code paths unchanged, no public API changes; dependency: g++/rustc/gcc toolchains already measured and pinned; concurrency: codegen edits single-threaded in one compiler process, no new threads; state: ledger and benchmark history stay append-only with the existing atomic-write discipline
impact_assessment.mitigation: every change gets a failing-first byte test plus an end-to-end wrap model test; G-004 re-runs all 12 benchmarks after every change with byte-identity proof when no codegen change is claimed; flagged noise is re-run before being treated as regression

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: flag-fused conditions -- route (x & literal) == 0 / != 0 and x == 0 / x != 0 and small-literal comparison branches straight from test/cmp flags to jcc, deleting the setcc/movzx/test round-trip (7 instr -> 2-4); plus eliding branch-to-next instructions that _emit_if emits when the condition target label sits at the current address. Targets: binary_gcd shift loops, nqueens bit scans, xorshift parity; measured with the ADR-028 --save --compare watch

impact_assessment.why: ADR-027 recorded the exact mechanism (bgcd pays setcc/movzx/test/branch where gcc tests flags) and binary_gcd/nqueens remain behind C and Rust
impact_assessment.benefits: fewer instructions and a shorter dependency chain in every hot bit-test loop; all three open scoreboard pairings benefit
impact_assessment.risks: contract: pure branch lowering, no semantics change if the flag routing is exact (== 0 -> jz, != 0 -> jnz); dependency: test_imm maxes at 127 so literals above it need the reg path; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first branch-shape tests; full suite + twin-parity; ADR-028 --save --compare before commit, revert if worse

Phase 4 verified: suite 400+39 green at a538dcd, cairn strict gate 4/4, compare exit 0; committed perf(codegen) fuse bit-test and logical conditions
Phase 4 checklist outcome: suite 400+39 green at a538dcd, aikit check cairn --strict 4/4 passed, secrets and README gates passed, benchmark compare exit 0

impact_assessment.why: The scoreboard rests on eight cases; whole bottleneck classes (multiply-latency chains, three-argument recursion, division-heavy nested loops, fixed-point inner escapes) are unmeasured, so the next optimizations risk overfitting to measured paths.
impact_assessment.benefits: Four new triple-twin benchmarks extend coverage to tak, primes, mandelbrot and splitmix, and each new case is permanently gated by the twin-parity and regression-watch machinery.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CASES tuple and TwinParityTest gain entries only, no pipeline contract changes; dependency: only the already-discovered gcc and rustc toolchains; concurrency: none, the harness is sequential; state: .aikit/benchmark_history.jsonl gains new-case records only and --compare claims nothing about cases seen for the first time. Language-semantics drift (signed overflow in C, arithmetic shift) is contained by uint64_t accumulators in the C twin where wrapping is load-bearing.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Twin-parity tests hard-fail on stdout divergence between the three languages; each triple is compiled and executed manually before entering CASES; loads are tuned to tens of milliseconds before baselines are saved.

checkpoints.description: [2/3-and-3/3 scope] Four twins written and parity-verified; operand-park miscompilation found by splitmix and fixed failing-first (GENERIC_EVAL_REGISTERS guard in _emit_binary_into); suite 425+39 green; baselines saved and compared exit 0; ADR-030 + README + KB done
Phase 4 checklist outcome: suite 425+39 green at d4cc6c6, aikit check cairn --strict 4/4 passed, twin parity for all 12 cases passed, benchmark --save --compare exit 0

impact_assessment.why: splitmix measures 165.9 ms against C's 98.7: per-iteration rematerialization of loop-invariant movabs constants is the recorded gap, and hoisting them is the next mechanism on the board.
impact_assessment.benefits: Removes per-iteration movabs/immediate loads for constants that never change across a loop body, closing part of the multiply-latency gap and potentially lifting primes and mandelbrot too.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: hoisting is confined to loop-body lowering of pure constant subexpressions, no statement contract changes; dependency: none beyond existing codegen structures; concurrency: none; state: no persistent state touched. Hoisting a constant whose evaluation could trap or diverge would change semantics, so only call-free, trap-free, division-free pure trees qualify; the regression watch flags any case that loses more than the noise band.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first e2e tests pin wraparound values at every hoist site; the twin-parity and regression-watch gates re-verify all 12 cases before any commit lands.

impact_assessment.why: The user's standing goal is that Cairn measures faster than C, C++ and Rust; the scoreboard only measures C (gcc/clang/cl) and Rust (rustc) today, so the claim cannot be tested for C++ at all. contract: additive Case field and new report keys only, existing fields and exit codes unchanged. dependency: C++ compilers already installed (g++ or clang++ or cl) detected the same way as the C row; no new toolchain requirement when absent - C++ verdicts read unavailable. concurrency: single-threaded harness, unchanged. state: history records gain a cpp key; compare_runs reads only the Cairn column, so old records stay comparable.
impact_assessment.benefits: The goal line gains a third verdict per case; 12 .cpp twins widen the parity gate; any C++-vs-C performance split that gcc's C++ frontend produces becomes visible and optimizable.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the TwinParityTest shape changes from triples to quadruples - old tests must keep passing until updated in the same commit. dependency: a broken or exotic C++ installation must degrade to unavailable, never crash the harness. concurrency: none. state: malformed cpp key in history must be skipped like the other baseline keys.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Additive-only schema change with the C build plumbing mirrored; parity gate run before any scoreboard number is recorded; absence of a C++ compiler returns unavailable verdicts and exit 2 only when no baseline at all exists
